scope: Category 7 only; read-only visual critique with report outputs. No native process, scene, code or runtime edits.
category_name: Purposeful worker traces and coercive institutional storytelling
overall_99_gate: Not evaluated by this specialist; this category failure blocks overall acceptance regardless of mean.
verdict: FAIL category threshold; no category-specific critical visual veto identified.
rationale: Arrival, inspection, check-in, evidence retention and concealed transfer are coherent. Numbered admission, contradictory reassurance, custody/retention cues and a restrained covered trolley create a specific coercive institution. Worker traces and physical use are weaker: orderly pale paperwork, a generic mug/workstation and broad immaculate contact surfaces do not yet communicate enough stressed daily use or maintenance under pressure for the strict gate.
inspection_method: Each of the 27 current PNGs and 4 spawn-reference PNGs was individually opened using tools.view_image. No contact-sheet substitution; rendered labels excluded as environmental story evidence.

pixel_evidence.finding: The protected speaking grille, tethered pen, stamp/ink pad, separate staff door and key box support a controlled admission procedure. STATE YOUR NUMBER is readable; WE VALUE YOUR TIME / ALL DELAYS ARE YOUR RESPONSIBILITY is a legible reassurance/coercion contradiction.
Scanner arch, closed cart gate, sealed arrival doors and disciplined lane markings make inspection and restricted movement understandable before reading small text.

The cargo box has a readable SECTOR 04 / CUSTODY 731-A label and yellow seal. The storage note reads DO NOT RELEASE with a partly occluded numbered record; locks and tape reinforce retention. The exact complete storage identifier cannot be certified from these pixels.
pixel_evidence.assessment: Purposeful custody/retention theme, more specific than filler labels; the full cross-object case match is not reliably readable.

pixel_evidence.finding: A covered, strapped trolley with an IV-style pole sits behind the office partition beside locked storage. The cover and hidden location make an unsettling transfer/concealment implication without exposing a body.
pixel_evidence.assessment: Strong bleak implication, although the transfer tag is too small/dark to add a specific procedural story.

pixel_evidence.finding: Mug, keyboard, angled chair, folders and forms establish ongoing staff work. Forms look largely pale and orderly, and the workstation has little distinctive history or interrupted activity.
pixel_evidence.assessment: Human presence is present but generic; worker pressure is underdeveloped.

pixel_evidence.finding: Small route-marking abrasion, a hanging service tag, mild counter/door marks and a little storage wear are visible. Large touch surfaces, gate panels, floor routes and office props remain very even and clean.
pixel_evidence.assessment: Localized use exists, but repairs/deterioration under pressure are not clearly earned at ordinary view distance.

pixel_evidence.finding: The sparse YOUR WORK MATTERS poster and factory graphic are readable at the heading level; its lower copy is not reliably legible in the supplied player view.
pixel_evidence.assessment: Restraint is good; this graphic supplies limited second-read specificity.

bounded_repair_targets.target: Existing check-in paperwork and stamp cluster
bounded_repair_targets.action: Replace the clean/light generic form read with one visibly processed or returned sheet: a short legible rejection/hold field, an offset stamp impression, one folded corner and selective ink/handling marks. Keep all objects within the existing counter footprint and preserve the hatch and prop poses.
bounded_repair_targets.success: The normal detail view shows an interrupted bureaucratic action and its consequence without another wall sign.

bounded_repair_targets.target: Existing counter, scanner threshold and cart-gate contact surfaces
bounded_repair_targets.action: Concentrate restrained wear where work causes it: wrist/clipboard rubbing on the counter edge, stamp-pad use, shoe turn marks at the threshold, and cart impact/scuffing on the lower gate contact band. Add one small credible existing-surface repair, avoiding blanket grime.
bounded_repair_targets.success: Wear forms a readable causal path from queue to processing to inspection; the room still reads active and maintained.

bounded_repair_targets.action: Develop one current work item and one modest personal trace inside the existing desk footprint: for example, a used case sheet with a marked unresolved field, plus a small worn personal card beside the monitor or a visibly repaired mug. Preserve desk/chair poses and circulation.
bounded_repair_targets.success: The desk suggests a particular tired worker handling unfinished business rather than a generic office-prop kit.

bounded_repair_targets.target: Existing covered-trolley docket and evidence note
bounded_repair_targets.action: Make the existing transfer docket contrast and short hold/status line readable from its current hero view, and connect it to the already visible 731-A custody record. Use typography/ink contrast on the existing surfaces; preserve trolley/cover/strap poses and avoid new props or explicit body exposure.
bounded_repair_targets.success: The concealment bay gains one clear, unsettling procedural connection while retaining ambiguity and negative space.
